partner_context.their_ambition: You are Dott — Europe and the Middle East's largest shared micromobility operator (the merged TIER-Dott), running 250,000 e-scooters and e-bikes across 400+ cities in 21 countries. You won the street layer city by city, tender by tender, on an operations-first, city-partnership model.
partner_context.their_pressure: Micromobility margins are won on utilization and city relationships — and the next differentiated surface is scarce. Streets are contested; the water in front of those same cities is empty. Every waterfront city you serve moves millions across bays, straits and archipelagos on slow diesel hulls, none of it in your app.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier gives Dott the water tier: a software-defined foiling fleet operating pier-to-pier in the cities Dott already serves — the same city-partnership playbook, extended to the harbour. Street fleet feeds pier; pier feeds street fleet.

hero.title: Dott × Navier — from the street layer to the water layer
hero.subtitle: Dott runs the streets of 400+ cities across Europe and the Middle East. The water between them is the one leg the app can't offer yet.
hero.what_we_do_together: We launch a Dott-integrated foiling water tier across Dott's waterfront markets. Navier brings the software-defined hydrofoiling fleet and the network playbook now proven in the Maldives; Dott brings the app, the riders, the city relationships and a street fleet at every pier. Together we make the water crossing one more leg of the journey Dott already serves.

why_now: Foiling lifts the hull clear of the water: faster, dramatically more efficient per passenger-mile, smooth and near-silent, hybrid-capable with no charging dependency, and autonomy-ready. A ~100-vessel network is already ramping in the Maldives — and the waterfront cities Dott serves from the Baltic to the Gulf still move by slow diesel ferry or not at all.

network_thesis.headline: Dott owns the street layer from the Baltic to the Gulf. The water layer is next.
network_thesis.body: Dott — Europe and the Middle East's largest shared micromobility operator (the merged TIER-Dott), running 250,000 e-scooters and e-bikes across 400+ cities in 21 countries. Its riders start and end their days in exactly the places Navier serves — marina districts, corniches, island quays, archipelago piers. A Navier foiling tier extends the same app from the street to the water: silent, all-electric, zero-wake crossings booked in the Dott app, with a Dott vehicle waiting at both piers.

network_thesis.coverage_note: Beyond the seven proposed markets, Dott's footprint covers waterfront cities across Poland's Baltic coast (Gdansk, Gdynia, Sopot), Denmark (Copenhagen), Germany's north coast (Hamburg, Kiel, Rostock), Swiss lakes, the UK (Bristol, Glasgow), Norway (Trondheim) and Israel's Mediterranean strip — each a natural extension as corridors are mapped.

multimodal_fit: Dott's e-scooters and e-bikes already saturate the streets on both sides of every crossing. The pier becomes another node in the same app: ride a Dott scooter to the quay, fly the crossing, pick up a Dott e-bike on the far side. No other operator can stage the first and last hundred metres of a water journey the way Dott can.

close.title: The water layer of Dott's cities.
close.body: From the Baltic to the Gulf, Dott already owns the street layer of Europe's waterfront cities. The water layer is next — same app, same rider, same city partnership model.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open water and the marinas and piers already in use. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all.
why_navier_now.the_moment: The technology crossed from prototype to platform (10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 sold out), decarbonization mandates turned diesel fleets into liabilities, and the hybrid removed the range excuse. The marine layer is being claimed cluster-by-cluster right now.

end_state.headline: The water layer of Dott's waterfront cities.
end_state.addressable_footprint: Every water-bound market in the Dott footprint — the Greek islands, the Dalmatian coast, the Italian Riviera and lagoon, the Côte d'Azur, the UAE, Saudi's commercial Corniche, the Tagus estuary, Dublin Bay, Tallinn and the Gulf of Finland, Cyprus's south coast, the Stockholm archipelago, the Balearics and Costa Brava, the Romanian Black Sea, Helsinki, plus sovereign-data-only Israel and held Lebanon — wherever Dott demand meets the coastline.
end_state.scale: 17 markets · 27+ anchor regions · steady-state ceiling tracked in partner sheet
end_state.narrative: Steady state is a Dott water tier spanning the Mediterranean, the Atlantic edge, the Baltic and the Gulf: book a foiling vessel the same way you book a car, from Athens to Dubai to Lisbon to Tallinn.

objections.concern: Ground ride-hail is our core — why move onto water?
objections.response: Water is the one urban surface Dott's mission of cheaper, cleaner, car-free mobility hasn't reached. Across the Saronic, the Dalmatian coast and the Gulf, the sea is the fastest line between two points — and no super-app owns it yet.

objections.concern: Is the range enough for the Mediterranean and Gulf?
objections.response: Most coastal and island hops are short — inside the all-electric Pioneer II's 70 nm envelope. The Quanta-LR hybrid covers the longer island and cross-gulf legs up to 700 nm with no charging infrastructure required.

objections.concern: We operate in 45+ countries — how do we launch without huge overhead?
objections.response: You don't build or run the fleet. Navier brings vessels, captains and maintenance; Dott brings demand, dispatch, the wallet and the brand. Each coastal city is a self-contained pilot on existing berths — no new infrastructure.

objections.concern: Will a water tier fit Dott's value positioning?
objections.response: Foiling's low energy per passenger-mile is exactly what makes an affordable water option viable. It's cleaner and car-free — on-brand for Dott — and the resort corridors fund the launch while commuters get a faster crossing.

objections.concern: You run scooters, not boats.
objections.response: So did no one, until now — the operating model is the same one you've mastered: dense urban fleets, app dispatch, city tenders, utilization economics. Navier supplies the hulls, captains and certification; you supply the city.

markets.label: Finland — Helsinki & Gulf of Finland
markets.summary: Helsinki sits on an archipelago: the city's islands — Suomenlinna, Lonna, Pihlajasaari, Korkeasaari — and the fast-growing Laajasalo/Kruunuvuorenranta waterfront are all short hops from the market square, served today by slow diesel ferries.

hero.title: Dott × Navier — Helsinki's archipelago shuttle
hero.subtitle: Foil to Suomenlinna and the islands at commuter speed, booked in the Dott app.
hero.what_we_do_together: A Dott-branded electric-foiling tier across Helsinki's inner archipelago and the Laajasalo waterfront, replacing slow diesel ferries on the city's busiest short-water commutes and tourist runs.

markets.why_now: Helsinki's archipelago carries millions of ferry trips a year — Suomenlinna alone draws ~1M+ visitors — on diesel ferries that are slow and timetable-bound. The new Kruunuvuorenranta/Laajasalo district is adding waterfront commuters. Pioneer II is commercial now and every inner-archipelago leg is well under its range.
markets.multimodal_fit: Dott's e-scooters and e-bikes already saturate the streets on both sides of every crossing — the pier becomes another node in the same app, so the water leg is door-to-door: ride to the pier, fly the crossing, ride onward.
markets.partner_context: Dott — Europe and the Middle East's largest shared micromobility operator (the merged TIER-Dott), running 250,000 e-scooters and e-bikes across 400+ cities in 21 countries. Dott runs the streets of 400+ cities across Europe and the Middle East — including the cities around Helsinki's archipelago waterfront. The water between them is the one leg the app can't offer yet; a Navier foiling tier makes it booked in the Dott app.

why_navier_now.narrative: Every Helsinki leg is tiny by water (Suomenlinna 1.5nm, Laajasalo 2nm), squarely inside Pioneer II's commercial envelope. The Helsinki–Tallinn crossing (43nm) is also within Pioneer range, making the Gulf-of-Finland link a real near-term corridor rather than a roadmap aspiration.

markets.differentiation: Against the diesel ferry: faster, quiet, all-electric and on-demand rather than fixed-timetable. Against the road: there is no road — the water is the only direct path, and we make it fast.

proof_points.claim: Dott is Europe and the Middle East's largest shared micromobility operator.
proof_points.evidence: The merged TIER-Dott runs 250,000 e-scooters and e-bikes across 400+ cities in 21 countries — from Helsinki to Dubai, Gdansk to Tenerife.
proof_points.source: Dott locations page + TIER-Dott merger announcements (2024–2026)

proof_points.evidence: Suomenlinna alone draws ~1M+ annual visitors; the inner islands carry millions of ferry trips a year.

proof_points.claim: The legs are short and dense.
proof_points.evidence: Market Square–Suomenlinna ~1.5nm, Helsinki–Laajasalo ~2nm — ideal Pioneer II corridors.

proof_points.claim: The Tallinn crossing is in Pioneer range.
proof_points.evidence: Helsinki–Tallinn is ~43nm, within Pioneer II's 70nm envelope — a near-term Gulf corridor, not roadmap.

proof_points.claim: Helsinki has strong decarbonization pull.
proof_points.evidence: City carbon-neutrality targets favour all-electric marine over diesel ferries.

objections.concern: Helsinki winters freeze the harbour.
objections.response: True — this is a strong shoulder/summer service. We right-size the fleet seasonally and concentrate on the high-demand ice-free months; the model assumes a seasonal, not year-round, operating window.

objections.concern: Public ferries already serve these islands cheaply.
objections.response: We don't replace the public ferry; we add a premium speed-and-frequency tier in the Dott app for riders who value time, plus the cross-Gulf Tallinn corridor the ferries serve slowly.

objections.concern: The Tallinn run sounds long for an 8-pax boat.
objections.response: It's 43nm — inside Pioneer II's 70nm range — so it's a genuine Phase-3 corridor, not a faked long leg.

markets.the_ask: Co-brand a water tier with Dott across Helsinki's archipelago waterfront, starting with a small Prove fleet on the shortest, densest hops and scaling as berth agreements land — every leg booked in the Dott app.
markets.close: Helsinki is a city built on water with a million-plus ferry trips a year on diesel boats — a clean, fast, in-app foiling tier is an obvious win for Dott and for the city's climate goals.
markets.end_state: A Helsinki archipelago network plus a Pioneer-range Gulf-of-Finland link to Tallinn, all booked in the Dott app.

Anchor on the Cannes/Antibes yacht hubs, scale through the Nice gateway and Monaco with the Nice Airport–Monaco corporate run, and reach St-Tropez and the cross-border Sanremo/Portofino legs. Dott's French presence is the front door.

markets.label: Greece — Saronic & Cyclades
markets.summary: Greece pairs the Athens Riviera commuter coast with the world's most iconic island-hopping market — the Saronic and Cyclades. Short inter-island hops (Mykonos–Delos, Naxos–Paros) and the Athens–Glyfada–Vouliagmeni coast are dense, premium, and underserved by slow ferries. Dott's strong Greek ridehail brand is the natural front door.

hero.title: Dott × Navier — Greece, the Aegean shuttle
hero.subtitle: Foil the Cyclades and the Athens Riviera at speed, booked in the Dott app.
hero.what_we_do_together: A Dott-branded electric-foiling tier across the Athens Riviera and the dense inter-island Cyclades and Saronic hops, with a roadmap leg across to the Turkish coast.

markets.why_now: Greece draws ~30M+ visitors a year, overwhelmingly to islands reached today by slow diesel ferries on fixed timetables. The Athens Riviera (Glyfada, Vouliagmeni) is a dense affluent commuter coast. Pioneer II is commercial now and clears the short inter-island and Riviera legs.
markets.multimodal_fit: Dott's e-scooters and e-bikes already saturate the streets on both sides of every crossing — the pier becomes another node in the same app, so the water leg is door-to-door: ride to the pier, fly the crossing, ride onward.
markets.partner_context: Dott — Europe and the Middle East's largest shared micromobility operator (the merged TIER-Dott), running 250,000 e-scooters and e-bikes across 400+ cities in 21 countries. Dott runs the streets of 400+ cities across Europe and the Middle East — including the cities around Athens' Saronic gulf and the island gateways. The water between them is the one leg the app can't offer yet; a Navier foiling tier makes it booked in the Dott app.

why_navier_now.narrative: The short inter-island and Riviera legs (Mykonos–Delos 3.5nm, Naxos–Paros 6nm, Piraeus–Glyfada 8nm) are squarely in Pioneer II range. The Rhodes–Marmaris crossing (22nm) is inside Pioneer range too; longer Aegean legs are staged on Quanta-LR, never faked.

markets.differentiation: Against the diesel ferry: faster, on-demand and not timetable-bound, with zero local emissions in protected Aegean waters. Against the road on the Riviera: a direct, scenic coastal line.

proof_points.claim: Dott is Europe and the Middle East's largest shared micromobility operator.
proof_points.evidence: The merged TIER-Dott runs 250,000 e-scooters and e-bikes across 400+ cities in 21 countries — from Helsinki to Dubai, Gdansk to Tenerife.
proof_points.source: Dott locations page + TIER-Dott merger announcements (2024–2026)

objections.response: We add a premium, fast, on-demand tier in the Dott app for time-sensitive riders, complementing — not replacing — the mass ferries.

objections.concern: The market is seasonal.
objections.response: Peak is summer, but the Athens Riviera commute and shoulder-season island demand extend operability; we right-size the fleet to the season.

markets.close: Greece is the iconic island market where the ferry is the bottleneck — a Dott-branded foiling tier turns the Aegean hop into the fastest, cleanest leg of every trip.

markets.label: Saudi Arabia — Jeddah & Eastern Province
markets.summary: Saudi Arabia's two commercial waterfront metros — Jeddah on the Red Sea and the Eastern Province (Dammam / Khobar / Dhahran) on the Arabian Gulf — are dense, high-income urban-water markets served today only by congested coastal roads. Jeddah's Corniche and the new PIF waterfront are a continuous urban seafront; the Eastern Province corniche, Half Moon Bay and Tarout Island sit minutes apart by water but a slow drive apart by road, with Bahrain a short cross-Gulf hop away. This is a clean two-metro rollout — Jeddah first, then the Eastern Province — on a purpose-fit premium water tier, booked in the Dott app.

markets.why_now: Saudi Arabia's urban waterfronts are being rebuilt as walkable, mixed-use seafronts — the Jeddah Corniche and PIF's new Jeddah Central, and the Eastern Province corniche and island leisure belt. Both are dense, high-income, road-congested, and minutes apart by water. Pioneer II is commercial now and clears every leg in both metros, including the cross-Gulf Khobar–Manama hop. No giga-project timing risk: this is today's urban water in two proven cities.
markets.multimodal_fit: Dott's e-scooters and e-bikes already saturate the streets on both sides of every crossing — the pier becomes another node in the same app, so the water leg is door-to-door: ride to the pier, fly the crossing, ride onward.

Dott runs the streets of 400+ cities across Europe and the Middle East — including the cities around Jeddah's Red Sea corniche and Saudi Arabia's opening coast. The water between them is the one leg the app can't offer yet; a Navier foiling tier makes it booked in the Dott app.
markets.why_navier_now: Every leg is in Pioneer II range now: the Jeddah Corniche–Central seafront (2.4nm), the Jeddah Corniche–Yacht Club run (12nm), the Eastern Province corniche and island hops (8–13nm), and the cross-Gulf Khobar–Manama link (~18.6nm). markets.label: Spain — Balearics & Costa Brava
markets.summary: Spain is Europe's #1 leisure-boating and second-busiest tourism market, with the densest island-and-coast water demand in the western Med — the Balearics, the Costa Brava and the Costa del Sol — almost none of it earning revenue in-app.

hero.title: Dott × Navier — Spain, the western-Med island shuttle
hero.subtitle: Turn the Balearic and Costa crossings into a flying, in-app water tier.
hero.what_we_do_together: A Dott-branded foiling water tier across the Balearics, the Costa Brava and the Costa del Sol — booked in the same app as the car, all-electric, no wake, no diesel-ferry timetable.

markets.why_now: Spain hosts ~85M visitors a year and the Balearics alone draw ~16M; the islands are choking on diesel ferries and rental cars while Formentera, Mallorca and Ibiza tighten anchoring and emissions rules. A clean, quiet, on-demand foiling hop is exactly what the regulators and the resorts are asking for — and no super-app has the water leg.
markets.multimodal_fit: Dott's e-scooters and e-bikes already saturate the streets on both sides of every crossing — the pier becomes another node in the same app, so the water leg is door-to-door: ride to the pier, fly the crossing, ride onward.
markets.partner_context: Dott — Europe and the Middle East's largest shared micromobility operator (the merged TIER-Dott), running 250,000 e-scooters and e-bikes across 400+ cities in 21 countries. Dott runs the streets of 400+ cities across Europe and the Middle East — including the cities around the Balearics, the Costa Brava and the Costa del Sol. The water between them is the one leg the app can't offer yet; a Navier foiling tier makes it booked in the Dott app.

why_navier_now.narrative: Pioneer II is commercial now and clears the short Balearic and Costa hops on a single charge; the Palma–Ibiza–Menorca regional legs (75–130nm) come into reach with Quanta-LR on the 2026+ roadmap. Spain's berths already exist — Palma, Ibiza Town, Formentera (La Savina), Puerto Banús — so we need a pedestal, not a port.

markets.differentiation: Against the diesel fast-ferry: half the door-to-door time, zero wake into protected Posidonia seagrass zones, no fixed timetable, and a fare booked in an app riders already have. Against a private RIB charter: a fraction of the cost and fully electric.

proof_points.claim: Dott is Europe and the Middle East's largest shared micromobility operator.
proof_points.evidence: The merged TIER-Dott runs 250,000 e-scooters and e-bikes across 400+ cities in 21 countries — from Helsinki to Dubai, Gdansk to Tenerife.
proof_points.source: Dott locations page + TIER-Dott merger announcements (2024–2026)

proof_points.claim: The Balearics are a top global leisure-marine market.
proof_points.evidence: Mallorca, Ibiza, Menorca and Formentera draw ~16M visitors a year with intense inter-island and coast-to-island water demand.

proof_points.claim: The corridors are protected and emissions-sensitive.
proof_points.evidence: Formentera caps daily vehicles and the Balearic Posidonia decree restricts anchoring and wake — favouring a quiet, electric, foiling hull.

proof_points.claim: The berths already exist.
proof_points.evidence: Palma, Ibiza Town, La Savina (Formentera), Port de Sóller, Puerto Banús and Marbella are working harbours — Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal.

objections.concern: The Balearic crossings (Palma–Ibiza) are too long for an 8-pax foiler.
objections.response: Correct — those 75–130nm legs are explicitly Quanta-LR (roadmap), never faked on a Pioneer II. The near-term business is the dense ≤70nm island-and-coast capillary network where Pioneer II is commercial today.

objections.concern: Ferries already run these routes.
objections.response: On fixed timetables, with diesel wake into protected zones, and no door-to-door app booking. The foiling hop wins on time, experience and emissions, and is bookable on demand in the Dott app.

objections.concern: Seasonality — Spain's water demand is summer-heavy.
objections.response: True, and the model sizes the Prove fleet to the shoulder-season floor; summer is upside. The same hulls redeploy across the Med as the network grows.

markets.the_ask: Co-brand a water tier with Dott across the Balearics, the Costa Brava and the Costa del Sol, starting with a small Prove fleet on the shortest, densest hops and scaling as berth agreements land — every leg booked in the Dott app.
markets.close: The water tier is the one leg no one has flown — let's fly it.
markets.end_state: A western-Med foiling network — Costa Brava, Costa del Sol and the Balearics — booked in the Dott app, with Quanta-LR closing the inter-island regional legs.

markets.label: UAE — Dubai & Abu Dhabi
markets.summary: The UAE is the anchor market: Dubai's jetty-dense waterfront (Palm, Dubai Harbour, Bluewaters, La Mer) plus the Dubai–Abu Dhabi corridor form the densest premium water-mobility opportunity in the network. Dott's regional ambition meets a market already conditioned to on-demand luxury transfers.

hero.title: Dott × Navier — UAE, the anchor market
hero.subtitle: Foil between Dubai's jetties and on to Abu Dhabi, booked in the Dott app.
hero.what_we_do_together: A Dott-branded electric-foiling tier across Dubai's jetty network, scaling to a Dubai–Abu Dhabi regional corridor — the flagship of the Dott water network.

markets.why_now: Dubai has the world's densest cluster of luxury hotel and residence jetties, a government actively promoting marine transport, and a clientele that already pays for premium transfers. The Dubai–Abu Dhabi road is a 90-minute-plus drive the water can shortcut. Pioneer II is commercial now and clears every intra-Dubai jetty hop.
markets.multimodal_fit: Dott's e-scooters and e-bikes already saturate the streets on both sides of every crossing — the pier becomes another node in the same app, so the water leg is door-to-door: ride to the pier, fly the crossing, ride onward.
markets.partner_context: Dott — Europe and the Middle East's largest shared micromobility operator (the merged TIER-Dott), running 250,000 e-scooters and e-bikes across 400+ cities in 21 countries. Dott runs the streets of 400+ cities across Europe and the Middle East — including the cities around Dubai's marina-and-canal metro and the wider Gulf shore. The water between them is the one leg the app can't offer yet; a Navier foiling tier makes it booked in the Dott app.

why_navier_now.narrative: Every intra-Dubai jetty leg (0.5–1.2nm) is trivially inside Pioneer II range. The Dubai Marina–Abu Dhabi Corniche corridor (55.8nm) sits inside the 70nm Pioneer envelope — a genuine near-term regional run, not a roadmap aspiration.

markets.differentiation: Against the chauffeur car: comparable cost, far faster jetty-to-jetty, air-conditioned cabin and a skyline view with zero local emissions. Against the diesel water taxi: foiling-quiet, on-demand and in-app.

proof_points.claim: Dott is Europe and the Middle East's largest shared micromobility operator.
proof_points.evidence: The merged TIER-Dott runs 250,000 e-scooters and e-bikes across 400+ cities in 21 countries — from Helsinki to Dubai, Gdansk to Tenerife.
proof_points.source: Dott locations page + TIER-Dott merger announcements (2024–2026)

proof_points.claim: Dubai has the densest luxury-jetty network in the world.
proof_points.evidence: Palm Jumeirah, Dubai Harbour, Bluewaters and La Mer concentrate dozens of premium jetties within 1–2nm of each other.

proof_points.claim: Dubai–Abu Dhabi is a Pioneer-range regional corridor.
proof_points.evidence: Dubai Marina–Abu Dhabi Corniche is ~56nm, inside Pioneer II's 70nm envelope.

proof_points.claim: Government actively promotes marine mobility.
proof_points.evidence: Dubai's marine-transport agenda and abundant licensed marina infrastructure support a water tier.

proof_points.claim: High willingness-to-pay for premium transfers.
proof_points.evidence: An established luxury on-demand transfer market gives the strongest economics in the network.

objections.concern: Summer heat limits demand.
objections.response: Air-conditioned foiling cabins make water transfer more comfortable than open-deck alternatives, and premium indoor-to-indoor jetty transfers are most attractive precisely when it's hottest.

objections.concern: Dubai already has water taxis.
objections.response: We add a premium, foiling, all-electric on-demand tier in the Dott app — faster and quieter than the existing diesel water taxis, not a like-for-like substitute.

objections.concern: Abu Dhabi is far by water.
objections.response: At 56nm it's inside Pioneer II range — a genuine Phase-3 regional corridor, not a faked long leg.

markets.the_ask: Co-brand a water tier with Dott across Dubai's marina-and-canal metro and the wider Gulf shore, starting with a small Prove fleet on the shortest, densest hops and scaling as berth agreements land — every leg booked in the Dott app.
markets.close: The UAE is the highest-value, highest-readiness water-mobility market on earth — the natural anchor to prove Dott-on-water before the network replicates it.
markets.end_state: A dense Dubai jetty network plus a Dubai–Abu Dhabi regional corridor, the flagship of the Dott water network.
